citation.authors: Lamon S, Morabito A, Arentson-Lantz E, Knowles O, Vincent GE, Condo D, Alexander SE, Garnham A, Paddon-Jones D, Aisbett B
citation.title: The effect of acute sleep deprivation on skeletal muscle protein synthesis and the hormonal environment

reported.what: postprandial mixed muscle fractional synthesis rate (FSR), one night of sleep deprivation (DEP) against the normal night (CON), mean ± SD, n = 13, measured between 13:00 and 15:00 (Results 3.2)

location.quote: Sleep deprivation reduced postprandial muscle protein fractional synthesis rate (FSR) by 18% (CON: 0.072 ± 0.015% vs. DEP: 0.059 ± 0.014%·h‐1, p = .040)

reported.what: plasma cortisol area under the curve 10:00 to 16:00, DEP against CON, mean ± SD, n = 13, in arbitrary units (AU)

location.quote: Plasma cortisol area under the curve (10:00–16:00), was 21% higher during DEP than CON (CON: 186 ± 41.7 AU vs. DEP: 226 ± 44.6 AU, p = .011)

reported.what: plasma testosterone area under the curve, DEP against CON, mean ± SD, n = 13, in arbitrary units (AU)

location.quote: The area under the curve decreased by 24% in the DEP condition (CON: 6.40 ± 5.28 AU vs. DEP: 4.86 ± 3.64 AU, p = .029

detail: The primary outcome, the postprandial muscle protein fractional synthesis rate, is a quantity the model has no state for, and the cortisol and testosterone areas are printed in arbitrary units that the loader cannot convert.
